title: EIP-8502: Dynamic individual consolidation incentive
description: Encourage consolidation with a per-validator balance deduction that rises while the validator count is above a scheduled target.
author: Anders Elowsson (@anderselowsson)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract This EIP encourages stakers to consolidate their stake into fewer validators to reduce the network load from carrying and aggregating votes. Each epoch, an individual consolidation incentive is subtracted from validator balances. It makes each additional validator carry a private cost, giving stakers a reason to reduce the public cost they impose on the network. The incentive is largest for 32-ETH validators, up to their attestation reward at full participation, and falls linearly with effective balance to zero at 2048 ETH. Every validator removed through consolidation therefore saves the staker about the same amount. The protocol lowers the target validator count at a constant rate over a predetermined period, then holds it fixed at a terminal target value. Starting from zero, the incentive rises gradually while the validator count is above target and falls ten times faster while it is below. ## Motivation Ethereum takes about 13 minutes to finalize a block, and proposals for faster finality aim to bring this down to a few slots. Typically, every validator votes in each finality round, and finality requires votes from validators holding two-thirds of the stake. Since any validator may be part of that two-thirds, the network must carry and aggregate votes from the whole validator set in every round. The cost grows with the number of validators, not with the amount of stake. At the time of writing, Ethereum has around 815,000 validators, making the validator count a central obstacle to faster finality. Post-quantum signatures, which are larger and costlier to aggregate, will raise the cost further and also put pressure on the current protocol. [EIP-7251](./eip-7251.md) lets stakers consolidate up to 2048 ETH into one validator, and large operators have begun to do so, but the average validator still holds only about 54 ETH. Consolidation is voluntary, and the protocol pays a 32-ETH validator the same yield per ETH as a 2048-ETH validator. With FOCIL ([EIP-7805](./eip-7805.md)), small validators may even earn more. Includers are selected per validator rather than per ETH, so a 32-ETH validator serves as includer 64 times as often per ETH as a 2048-ETH validator, and an includer may charge fees out of band for listing transactions in its inclusion list. Not consolidating therefore has a public cost, since the network must carry the votes of every validator, but little or no private cost. Nothing ensures that the validator count falls to a level that allows a clean fast-finality design, or that it stays there as new stake arrives. This EIP adds a dynamic individual consolidation incentive. The protocol publishes a schedule for the validator count that falls linearly toward a terminal target. As long as consolidation keeps pace with the schedule, nothing changes. If it lags, an individual incentive is subtracted from validators' balances each epoch, largest for the smallest validators and zero at 2048 ETH. Not consolidating then carries a private cost. How large an incentive each operator needs before it consolidates is knowledge dispersed among stakers and unavailable to protocol designers. The incentive therefore acts as a price rather than a fixed penalty. It rises only while consolidation lags the schedule, so the operators who can consolidate most cheaply move first, and it falls while the validator count is below the schedule. Each additional validator costs its operator about the same amount, so the price falls on the resource that a fast-finality design must economize: validators. ## Specification ### Parameters | Name | Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `FORK_EPOCH` | TBD | Activation epoch | | `VALIDATOR_TARGET_START` | TBD, e.g. `2**19` | Target at ramp start | | `VALIDATOR_TARGET_END` | TBD, e.g. `2**17` | Terminal target | | `VALIDATOR_TARGET_RAMP_DURATION_MS` | `47_304_000_000` | Ramp, 1.5 years | | `CONSOLIDATION_FORCE_RISE_TIME_MS` | `25_920_000_000` | Rise time $\tau_{\uparrow}$, 300 days | | `CONSOLIDATION_FORCE_FALL_TIME_MS` | `2_592_000_000` | Fall time $\tau_{\downarrow}$, 30 days | | `CONSOLIDATION_FORCE_DENOMINATOR` | `10**9` | Force at 100% | ### Beacon state ```python class BeaconState(ProgressiveContainer): ACTIVE_FIELDS = active_fields(width=47, gaps=(8, 9, 10, 28)) # [Modified in this EIP] # ... existing fields ... consolidation_force: Uint64 # [New in this EIP] in units of 1 / CONSOLIDATION_FORCE_DENOMINATOR ``` The new field is appended at index 46, after the last field of the Heze beacon state. The fork upgrade function MUST set `consolidation_force = 0`. ### Helper functions ```python def get_validator_target(state: BeaconState, time_ms: Uint64) -> Uint64: genesis_time_ms = seconds_to_milliseconds(state.genesis_time) start_ms = compute_time_at_slot_ms(genesis_time_ms, compute_start_slot_at_epoch(FORK_EPOCH)) elapsed = min(time_ms - start_ms, VALIDATOR_TARGET_RAMP_DURATION_MS) reduction = (VALIDATOR_TARGET_START - VALIDATOR_TARGET_END) * elapsed // VALIDATOR_TARGET_RAMP_DURATION_MS return Uint64(VALIDATOR_TARGET_START - reduction) ``` ```python def get_validator_count(state: BeaconState) -> Uint64: # Active validators, excluding sources of pending consolidations epoch = get_current_epoch(state) active = len(get_active_validator_indices(state, epoch)) consolidating = len([ c for c in state.pending_consolidations if is_active_validator(state.validators[c.source_index], epoch) ]) return Uint64(active - consolidating) ``` ```python def get_individual_consolidation_incentive(state: BeaconState, index: ValidatorIndex) -> Gwei: e_min = MIN_ACTIVATION_BALANCE // EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_INCREMENT e_max = MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_ELECTRA // EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_INCREMENT e = state.validators[index].effective_balance // EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_INCREMENT e = min(max(e, e_min), e_max) full_reward = get_base_reward(state, index) * sum(PARTICIPATION_FLAG_WEIGHTS) // WEIGHT_DENOMINATOR exposed = full_reward * e_min * (e_max - e) // (e * (e_max - e_min)) # full_reward * f(e)
